title: Can, could, be able to
goal: Talk about ability and possibility, now and in the past
wm: Auxiliary and Modal Verbs: Can, Could
intro: Modal verbs like can and could are followed by the base form of a verb, with no “to” and no -s: “She can drive.” Use “can” for ability now, “could” for general ability in the past, and “be able to” for the tenses that can’t use “can” (will be able to, have been able to).

rules.rule: can / can’t + base form: ability now.
could / couldn’t: ability in the past.
examples: I could swim when I was five.

rules.rule: be able to for other tenses.
examples: I’ll be able to help you tomorrow.
I haven’t been able to sleep.

mistakes.wrong: I can able to do it.
mistakes.right: I can do it. / I am able to do it.
mistakes.why: Use can OR be able to, not both.

mistakes.right: I will be able to come.

ex.q: I ___ ride a bike when I was six.
Will you ___ join the call later?
Sorry, I ___ hear you. The line is bad.
I am not able to can open this file.
ex.fixed: I am not able to open this file.
ex.y: Use one: I’m not able to open / I can’t open.

ex.q: We will can finish it by Friday.
ex.fixed: We will be able to finish it by Friday.

ex.q: When I was young, I ___ eat anything without getting fat.

ex.a: I haven't been able to call him.

ex.q: Correct this: “She can able to cook very well.”
a: She is able to cook very well
ex.y: Use can OR be able to.

talk: Talk about three things you can do well, two things you couldn’t do as a child but can now, and one thing you hope you’ll be able to do next year.
